status_summary: Secretary's Order 3433, signed 2025-06-23 and effective immediately, rescinds Order 3408 of 2022 in full and reinstates, with updates, Order 3368 of 2018. It directs the Solicitor's office and the Chief Information Officer to maintain a public Litigation Transparency Portal, post within 30 days a searchable list of consent decrees and settlements since fiscal year 2012 with associated attorneys' fee payments, and post final agreements within 15 days of execution. The Interior Solicitor's page lists a Litigation Transparency Portal among its resources, but the portal's contents (settlements, fee data, dates covered) could not be read, so whether it is populated as the order directs was not confirmed.

timeline.event: Interior issued Secretary's Order 3433, which rescinds Order 3408, reinstates Order 3368 with updates, and directs a public Litigation Transparency Portal listing consent decrees, settlements and attorneys' fee payments.

title: Reinstate the Interior policy on open access to litigation settlements and fees
uncertainties: In review the signed order was opened on doi.gov and read: section 5 rescinds Order 3408, reinstates Order 3368 with updates, requires the Litigation Transparency Portal with case-level details including fees and their source, requires 30-day comment periods for qualifying proposed settlements and posting of final agreements within 15 days, and certification of fee payments over $10,000; section 6 allows written waivers that must themselves be posted. The archived page for Order 3408 says it was canceled and replaced by Order 3433. Whether the portal has been published and populated was not confirmed; two web searches did not surface it. The order creates no enforceable rights and can be revoked by a later Secretary. On 2026-10-19 the Interior Solicitor page was fetched and its resources menu includes a Litigation Transparency Portal link pointing to a litigationtransparency subdomain of doi.gov; automated fetching of that subdomain was refused by its robots rules for both the researcher and the independent review, so its contents, entry count and update dates were not read. Four web searches (three by the researcher, one in review) found no news report or Interior release on the portal's launch or contents. The Solicitor page carries no visible date for the link (its metadata date is from 2015). The stage stays implemented because the order is operative and a portal link exists, and is not moved to completed because population of the portal is unverified.
